source: Khieu Borin, Than Soeurn, Preston T.R. and Sato K. 1996. The role of the sugar palm tree (Borassus flabellifer) in livestock based farming systems in Cambodia. In: Sustainable Livestock Production on Local Feed Resources, FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific (RAP Publication), Bangkok.
text: Sugar palm juice feeding works best as part of an integrated farming system rather than in isolation. Pig manure and waste can feed a biodigester (about 450 were installed across Cambodia at the time of this study, often paired with the household latrine), which produces methane gas for household cooking — cutting firewood costs and expenditure on chemical fertilizer — while the digester slurry is safe to use as fish-pond feed and provides better quality fertilizer for rice fields and vegetable gardens than fresh manure. Multipurpose trees and water plants such as Trichanthera gigantea, duckweed, water spinach, and azolla growing around the household can supply the protein side of the diet alongside the palm juice's energy. Pigs, chickens, and ducks are named as the priority animals for this system, and confining pigs (rather than free-ranging them) is specifically recommended because of their tendency to damage sweet potato and vegetable gardens.
